translations.whyIntro: Communication science and framing research demonstrate that how political actors are perceived is substantially shaped by the visual signals used to represent them in news formats.
translations.whyCard1: In colour psychology, blue is universally linked to calm, credibility, and objectivity. It is the hallmark colour of international peacekeeping bodies and European institutions. Adopting a party's self-chosen branding without critique creates a subconscious softening effect toward anti-constitutional tendencies.
translations.whyCard2: In Germany's political iconography, brown unambiguously signifies völkisch nationalism and right-wing extremism. Responsible information design should demonstrate the clarity to reflect ideological classifications visually.

translations.editorialPolicyIntro: This site follows an informational, documentation-led approach. To ensure clarity and accountability, our standards are transparently outlined:
translations.editorialPolicyRule1: Primary sources first: We prioritize direct links to scientific research, court rulings, and independent newsrooms.
translations.editorialPolicyRule2: Context over slogans: All topics are contextualized with dates, institutional background, and analytical depth.
translations.editorialPolicyRule3: Archive resilience: Wherever practical, key press reports and rulings are preserved via archive copies.
translations.editorialPolicyRule4: Analytical distance: Extremist terminology is deconstructed and analyzed, never uncritically amplified.
translations.editorialPolicyCorrectionsBody: If you identify a factual inaccuracy, please get in touch via the channels provided in the legal notice. Substantive notes will be verified and addressed promptly.

oeffentlich.to: TO: Editorial Boards of ARD-aktuell & ZDF
oeffentlich.subject: Re: Visual Framing and Journalistic Duty of Contextualization
body: Public service broadcasters bear a fundamental responsibility for impartial, accurately contextualized information for the public.

The uncritical adoption of the colour blue for a party classified in parts as proven right-wing extremist and unconstitutional conveys subtle associations of moderation and institutional respectability.
We therefore ask you to evaluate your visual guidelines and utilize representations in diagrams that visually reflect the documented radicalism of these movements.

privat.to: TO: Editorial Boards of ProSiebenSat.1, RTL Group & dpa
privat.subject: Re: Default Colour Standards in Infographic Feeds
body: Your newsrooms and agency feeds shape the daily perception of millions of viewers and readers across Germany.
When groups monitored and classified as extremist by security agencies are depicted in the same conventional blue as international institutions, a subconscious normalizing effect is produced.
We encourage you to critically assess your graphical standards and avoid the unexamined replication of far-right corporate identity design.

rundfunkrat.to: TO: ARD Broadcasting Councils & ZDF Television Council
rundfunkrat.subject: Re: Program Oversight Regarding Visual Framing Effects
body: As supervisory bodies of public broadcasting, you are tasked with safeguarding journalistic quality standards and balanced reporting.
Visual choices in news programmes profoundly guide public perception. Uncritically maintaining extremist actors within an unobtrusive default color spectrum falls short of this responsibility.
We urge you to initiate a dialogue on differentiated, fact-based visual designations within daily broadcast graphics.

faqs.q: Why is the party colour blue problematic here?
faqs.a: Psychologically, blue is associated with stability, calmness, and neutrality – it is the colour of both the UN and the EU. When media uncritically mirrors the self-branding of a party with proven extremist factions, this calming sentiment is unconsciously transferred to the public image of that party.

faqs.q: Wouldn't changing the colour violate journalistic neutrality?
faqs.a: No. Neutrality does not require the passive reproduction of political PR. Editorial desks routinely set colour standards according to clarity and contextual needs (such as using black for the CDU/CSU rather than turquoise). Visual framing is an integral part of editorial autonomy.

faqs.q: What is the goal of this initiative?
faqs.a: We aim to initiate a debate on media ethics regarding the impact of visual news graphics. The objective is to increase awareness that graphical design choices in newsrooms carry meaning and are never neutral.
A civil society initiative advocating for media ethics and democratic discourse quality, launched via Change.org.

science.sectionSub: Fact Sheet: Visual Framing and Editorial Autonomy in Political Reporting

foundations.title: The Psychological Dimension of "Visual Framing" (Halo Effect)

points.label: Colour Psychology of Blue
points.text: Empirical studies consistently find that blue hues elicit associations of seriousness, de-escalation, and dependability – the reason institutions like the UN and European bodies employ it.

points.label: Cognitive Dissonance in Charts
points.text: When an actor classified by security authorities as extremist is displayed in neutral cyan or calm blue, a normalizing halo effect takes place: the calming visual tone attenuates audience awareness of constitutional risks.

points.label: The taz Precedent
points.text: During past federal election cycles, the national daily taz made an editorial decision to depict AfD figures in distinct colors. This highlights that journalistic contextualization rightfully extends to graphic design.

points.label: Established Colour Conventions
points.text: Newsrooms regularly deviate from official party CI to ensure visual clarity (e.g., black for the Union rather than turquoise, distinct reds for SPD vs. The Left). Palette choice is an autonomous editorial tool.

objections.title: Objection 1: "The neutrality principle requires identical formal treatment."

rebuttals.label: Substantive vs. Purely Formal Balance
rebuttals.text: Constitutional jurisprudence requires media to provide substantive contextualization. Professional journalistic diligence entails pointing out differences in constitutional allegiance clearly and transparently.

rebuttals.label: Findings by Constitutional Protection Authorities
rebuttals.text: Court-confirmed classifications by intelligence and security agencies represent documented facts. Graphics reflecting this reality comply directly with the statutory duty for truthful reporting.

rebuttals.label: Broadcasting Freedom & Autonomy
rebuttals.text: Freedom of broadcasting under Art. 5(1)(2) of the Basic Law safeguards editorial departments from having to replicate the promotional concepts of political parties without scrutiny.

objections.title: Objection 2: "Media must follow the party's own brand identity."

rebuttals.label: The Obligation of Journalistic Distance
rebuttals.text: Party marketing serves partisan objectives. The principle of critical distance dictates maintaining independent editorial criteria rather than functioning as PR megaphones.

rebuttals.label: Clarity for the Public
rebuttals.text: Information graphics exist to provide orientation. A design practice that conceals radical agendas beneath innocuous standard palettes defeats this public service mandate.

objections.title: Objection 3: "This fuels the party's victimhood narrative."

rebuttals.label: Preemptive Strategic Rhetoric
rebuttals.text: Media studies verify that populist movements cultivate grievance narratives systematically – completely independent of actual editorial formatting choices.

rebuttals.label: Transparency over Hesitation
rebuttals.text: Journalistic determinations must not be suppressed out of fear of calculated backlash. Transparent, evidence-based reasoning is the strongest safeguard for editorial integrity.

policyDangers.title: Social & Welfare
policyDangers.description: Economic and social policy analyses indicate substantial disadvantages for low-wage earners, pensioners, and employees.
points: Rejection of statutory minimum wage increases, which disproportionately impacts economically vulnerable regions.
Proposals to drastically curb basic social security support in favor of mandatory community labour requirements.
Demands to eliminate wealth and inheritance taxes, primarily yielding tax relief for the highest income and wealth brackets.
policyDangers.citation: German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin) — The AfD Paradox (2023)

policyDangers.title: Economy & Prosperity
policyDangers.description: Protectionist nationalism and withdrawal from European integration undermine national economic vitality.
points: IW Calculation (2024): A German withdrawal from the EU ('Dexit') would reduce real GDP by approx. 5.6% (around €690 billion) within five years.
Exacerbation of skilled labour shortages through aggressive anti-immigration policies and international deterrence effects.
Unbudgeted tax reduction plans threaten the fiscal sustainability and investment capacity of public budgets.
policyDangers.citation: German Economic Institute (IW Cologne) — Consequences of an EU Exit (2024)

policyDangers.title: Press & Broadcasters
policyDangers.description: Recurring efforts to sideline critical journalists and undermine constitutionally protected press freedom.
points: Judicially overruled attempts to bar independent journalists from party conferences and election night coverage.
Targeted campaigns aimed at discrediting public service broadcasting and draining its funding structures.
Risks mirroring developments observed in illiberal systems where media diversity has been compromised.
policyDangers.citation: Erfurt District Court / Munich District Court I (2024) — Emergency decisions on press freedom

policyDangers.title: Art, Culture & Education
policyDangers.description: Attempts to politically restrict independent artistic, academic, and school initiatives.
points: Courts dismissed attacks against politically reflective theatre productions, reaffirming artistic freedom as a constitutional right.
Parliamentary motions attempting to condition cultural grants on ideological affirmations.
Initiatives promoting reporting portals aimed at monitoring teachers who critically address constitutional issues.
policyDangers.citation: Hanover Administrative Court (2023) / Federal Association of Free Performing Arts

policyDangers.title: Security & Violence
policyDangers.description: Official criminal statistics demonstrate a persistently elevated threat from politically motivated right-wing crime.
points: Offenses (2025): Around half of all politically motivated crimes are registered within the far-right spectrum.
Disproportionately elevated numbers in physical assaults, violent crimes, and targeted intimidation.
High volume of coordinated digital hate campaigns directed at civil society figures.
policyDangers.citation: Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA) — Politically Motivated Crime in 2025 (June 2026)

policyDangers.title: Alliances & Networks
policyDangers.description: Close ties to ultranationalist factions across Europe alongside ongoing inquiries into links with authoritarian regimes.
points: Key involvement in establishing the nationalist ESN faction within the European Parliament.
Investigations regarding financial networks and influence operations tied to pro-Russian platforms.
Security-relevant inquiries surrounding suspected intelligence collaborations.
policyDangers.citation: German Bundestag / Federal Public Prosecutor / Munich Prosecution (2024-2025)
